title: Pay for Consistency on a Healthy Day
description: There is no network partition. A team compares local replica reads with reads that wait for cross-region coordination. Which tradeoff does PACELC help explain?

options.text: Stronger coordination can improve consistency while adding latency.
options.explanation: The 'else' part of PACELC describes the latency-versus-consistency choice during normal operation, not just failures.

options.text: Without partitions, every replica is immediately current.
options.explanation: Asynchronous replication can lag on a healthy network, so read policy still matters.

options.text: Eventual consistency promises every replica catches up within two seconds.
options.explanation: It promises convergence under the model's conditions, not a fixed deadline unless the system adds one.

options.text: Read-your-writes requires all global reads to be linearizable.
options.explanation: A session can receive read-your-writes through routing or version checks without giving that guarantee to every reader.
